solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grand made a tidy sum kept at home

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
to round a figure up or down is to make it a tidy sum

explanation.surface: Someone has made a grand, a nice tidy sum, and kept the money at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like an adjective or a sum of money; it is only the letter G. 'Tidy sum' sounds like a lot of cash but here means a number rounded off.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager who is grounded is punished by being confined to the house, so kept at home fits exactly.

clue.text: A position with game in front of it

definitions.text: A position with game in front of it

indicators.note: something placed in front of another comes first, so this piece leads when written down

blocks.note: Go is the Japanese board game
A, plus a lie, the position a golf ball rests in

explanation.surface: Someone describes a spot on the field that has all the action ahead of it.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue is wordplay and definition at once. The lie of a ball is its resting position, a golfing sense; Go is the Japanese board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper stands at the back of the team, so every bit of play happens ahead of that player's spot.

clue.text: Unaware manifest includes lithium

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: manifest as an adjective means plain to see
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A shipping manifest lists lithium, and someone has not noticed the hazardous cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manifest' reads as a noun, a cargo list, which suits the lithium; it is the adjective meaning evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone oblivious to a thing has no knowledge or awareness of it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Not very musical group soon releasing covers

indicators.note: letting go of the covers strips off the outside, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians
the two middle letters of the word, once its ends go

explanation.surface: A not very musical band will soon be putting out cover versions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Releasing covers' pretends to be a band issuing cover songs; it means taking the outer letters off. A nonet is to nine what a quartet is to four.
explanation.definitionFit: 'None too happy' is an idiom meaning not especially happy, so the phrase is a mild negative equal to not very.

clue.text: Send cheque finally, after it’s due

indicators.note: what comes finally comes at the end, so only the closing letter is taken

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
anything arriving after it was due is late

explanation.surface: A reminder to finally send off a cheque now that the payment is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send' looks like an instruction about posting the cheque; it is the definition, in its older sense of thrilling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that sends you transports you with delight, an old slang sense matching to make someone joyful.

clue.text: Open prison was satisfactory

blocks.note: the can is slang for prison
as in 'that did' or 'that will do': it served well enough

explanation.surface: An open prison was judged to have been good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open prison' is a real British phrase for a low-security jail, so the two words seem to belong together; 'Open' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A candid person speaks frankly and hides nothing, which is being open in manner.

clue.text: Third man shares cell with fat old philosopher and lover

indicators.note: two words sharing one grid square overlap there, so their common letter is written only once

blocks.note: Abel was the third man in Genesis, after Adam and Cain
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A third prisoner is banged up with a fat old thinker and a romancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third man' calls up the film or a cricket fielder; it is Abel, the third person created. 'Cell' is a grid square, so the L is shared.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard was a twelfth-century French scholar famed for his tragic love affair with Héloïse.

clue.text: US drug agency officer sold drugs

blocks.note: the DEA is the American Drug Enforcement Administration
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A narcotics agent has been caught selling the very substances they were meant to seize.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug agency and the drug dealing sit in one scandal, so the clue looks like a news headline rather than two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer is someone who peddles narcotics, so to have dealt is past tense of that trade.

clue.text: Tiles hopefully all toppling in old cupola’s nets

indicators.note: a net catches and holds its catch inside, so one part is enclosed by another

blocks.note: the word used as it stands
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a cupola is a dome, and the 's stands for 'is' spelt as S

explanation.surface: Roof tiles are sliding off an old cupola and being caught in nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiles' suggests roofing, which suits the cupola; the definition is gaming pieces lined up so they fall in a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino rally sets small gaming pieces on end so that knocking one sends the whole row tumbling.

clue.text: Roman road, say, so few turns

indicators.note: something that turns changes its order and direction, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: eight letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A Roman road that runs so straight it barely bends at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface boasts of the famously straight Roman roads; the Fosse Way ran from Exeter to Lincoln across England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the major routes built across Britain during the Roman occupation, still followed by modern roads.

clue.text: While original a sermon’s interminable

indicators.note: an original version is novel and new, so the letters are made into something fresh

blocks.note: 'while' in the sense of provided that, or during the time that
seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: An original sermon is being praised while the congregation suffers through its endless length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' is an unusual signal: it means new, so the letters are given new form. The ’s is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A list 'as long as your arm' is an idiom for something very lengthy, seemingly without end.

clue.text: Guest wearing very informal shirt on island

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another is placed after it

blocks.note: dressed in something is wearing it
v is the abbreviation for very
I is the usual abbreviation for island
a tee is a T-shirt, a casual top

explanation.surface: A holiday guest turns up on the island in a very casual T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' seems to describe the guest's clothes; it only supplies IN. The shirt follows the island in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitee is someone who has been asked to attend, which is a guest by another name.

clue.text: Frugal bath was running — little time to fill that

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so one small piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a spa is a bath or a place for bathing
the past tense of run
T is the abbreviation for time, the smallness hinting at one letter

explanation.surface: A thrifty person runs a bath, but only allows a little time to fill it.
explanation.walkthrough: The running bath and filling it make a domestic scene; 'that' points back to RAN, which takes the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Spartans were famous for austere, simple living, so spartan means sparing and plain.

clue.text: Male depression son leaves for another day

indicators.note: whoever leaves goes away, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat
SORROW (depression) without S for son

explanation.surface: A depressed man's son moves out, and he hopes things will look up later.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes Scarlett O'Hara's 'tomorrow is another day', which gives the gloomy surface its hopeful ending. S for son is standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The day after today is literally a different one still to come, and the famous line pairs the two.

clue.text: Arabs during theology class convert to Catholicism

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within it, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: Omanis are people of Oman, an Arab country
RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: Some Arab students in a religion lesson decide to become Catholics.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is the British school subject; the whole scene stays inside a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To romanise is to bring someone under the Church of Rome, the Roman Catholic faith.

clue.text: Beneficiary agreed with judge’s conclusion

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: 'Done!' is said to seal an agreed deal
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An heir is pleased that the judge's final ruling went their way.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface suits the answer, a legal term; 'agreed' is the handshake word, as in 'it's a deal, done'.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a donee receives a gift from a donor, so is the one who gains from it.

clue.text: Bloodthirsty character unusual for Austen

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal run, so the letters appear in an odd order

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A literary critic notes that a violent character would be most unusual in a Jane Austen novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Austen's drawing-room novels make a vampire comically out of place, which is the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Orlok in the 1922 silent film Nosferatu is a vampire, a creature that feeds on blood.

clue.text: School dance I arrange, almost guaranteeing party

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a prom is a formal school dance
the letter as it stands
SORT (arrange) with its final T removed

explanation.surface: A student offers to organise the school dance and all but promises a great party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests the prom's celebration; here it is the legal sense, a side to a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: In a contract the promisor is the side that makes the undertaking, so that person is bound to deliver.

clue.text: Small state broadcaster likely to fail

blocks.note: RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state
Sky is a British satellite television company

explanation.surface: A small country's state broadcaster is expected to go under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small state broadcaster' reads as one public channel; it splits into Rhode Island and Sky, the British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture that is risky carries danger of going wrong, so failure is a real possibility.

clue.text: NY garden mature, length as measured

blocks.note: an American calls a garden a yard; NY signals the US usage
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A New York garden has grown established, and someone is pacing out its size.
explanation.walkthrough: NY is New York, standing for American English here, where the patch behind a house is a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance counted in yards, as in American football, so a length expressed in units.

clue.text: Municipal chairman’s wife hiding diamonds in dressing gown

indicators.note: whatever is hidden is put out of sight, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: mayo, short for mayonnaise, is a salad dressing
a dress is a gown
D is the abbreviation for the suit of diamonds in cards; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: The mayor's wife has stashed her diamonds in the pocket of her dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing gown' is a trap: the familiar phrase must be split into two separate words. 'Hiding' does not put one piece inside another here; it makes a letter vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoress is traditionally the spouse of a mayor, who heads a town or city council.

clue.text: Pictish tribe retreated northwards, embracing fresh start

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the words hold the answer inside them
retreating north in a down entry means travelling upward, so the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A defeated Pictish tribe fell back to the north of Scotland, hoping to begin again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Picts were an ancient people of Scotland who did retreat north before the Romans, so the history sounds real and hides the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebirth is a renewal or new beginning, the same idea as starting over afresh.

clue.text: Bond after the first Christmas present

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, counts years from the birth of Christ
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A spy like James Bond finally receives a Christmas present after the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas present' begs to be read as a gift; 'present' means here, and the first Christmas is the Nativity that dates AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue that bonds to a surface sticks to it, so to adhere is to stick fast.

clue.text: Golf club in the south of France Republican applied to

blocks.note: the Midi is the name for southern France
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a coat of paint applied to a wall is on it

explanation.surface: An American Republican joins a golf club on the French Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Golf club in' the south of France reads as a country club location; 'Golf club' alone is the definition, an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A midiron is an old name for a medium-lofted iron, the number two iron used for long approach shots.

clue.text: Current temperature lower than doctor provided

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is lower comes further down the column, so it is written after the rest

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
provided that means if
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A patient's temperature is now below what the doctor recorded earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current temperature' reads as a medical reading; 'Current' is the definition, a flow of water or air.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a slow movement carried along by water or wind, as in an ocean stream.

clue.text: Be opposite to but somehow inside ship

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the letters are put in any order
whatever is inside sits within the walls of something else

blocks.note: three letters of fodder
to ship goods is to send them

explanation.surface: Two things stand opposed, yet somehow end up together on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' is a noun in the surface and a verb in the wordplay. The definition is geometric.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a side of a triangle subtends the angle across from it, lying on the far side.

clue.text: Feathered hat it’s surprising king wears like that

indicators.note: a thing worn is put on around the wearer, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: 'do it so' means do it like that
ha! is an exclamation of surprise
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king in a plumed hat is a surprising sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King wears' makes the king the one in the hat; in fact SO wears HA and K.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall military cap, often topped with a plume or pompom.

clue.text: One wound up in the Tower, perhaps

definitions.text: One wound up in the Tower, perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: One wound up in the Tower
blocks.note: surface reading: a prisoner who ended up locked in the Tower of London
setter's reading: 'wound' as in winding, coiled round and round while rising inside a tower

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' sounds like finished up as a prisoner, and the Tower of London was a famous jail; really it means coiled, a set of steps turning round a central post.
explanation.definitionFit: Towers often contain steps that turn round a central column as they climb, a classic example.

clue.text: Desert lion scratching its back a bit

indicators.note: scratching out removes something, and the back is the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship
HERO (a lion, a brave person) without its final O

explanation.surface: A desert lion is having a bit of a scratch on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert lion' reads as one animal of the Sahara; 'Desert' is a verb, and a lion is a hero, as in a literary lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather cold means somewhat cold, so the adverb works as a modest degree.

clue.text: Stock structure of company which people exploit

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
who is the relative pronoun for people, as which is for things
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A description of a company's share structure that insiders exploit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock structure of company' reads as finance; stock here means livestock, and the structure is a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowhouse is a farm building sheltering cattle, which are livestock.
